title: Topic 63 | Work and power of a current source

questions.text: Which of the given formulas expresses the Joule–Lenz law?
A wire of resistance $2~\Omega$ carries a current of $15$ A. How much energy is released in it in $2$ minutes (kJ)?
What current must be passed through a conductor of resistance $50~\Omega$ for $10$ minutes for $120$ kJ of heat to be released (A)?
A conductor of resistance $12~\Omega$ is connected to a $120$ V mains. How much heat is released in the conductor in $10$ min?
If $R_1 = R_2 = R_3$, determine the ratio of the amounts of heat $Q_1 : Q_2 : Q_3$ released in the same time in the resistors shown in the figure.
Resistances $R$ and $2R$ are connected in parallel to a DC voltage source. In the resistance $R$, $100$ J of heat is released. How much heat is released in the resistance $2R$ (J)?

An electric kettle has two heating coils. When one of them is connected, the water in the kettle boils in $30$ minutes; when the other is connected, it boils in $20$ minutes. In how many minutes will the water in the kettle boil if both coils are connected in series?

An electric kettle with a heating coil resistance of $50~\Omega$ contains water at a temperature of $0^\circ$C with a volume of $600$ cm$^3$. How many minutes are needed to bring all the water to a boil and turn it into steam, if the mains voltage is $200$ V and the efficiency of the kettle is $60\%$? For water, $c=4.2$ kJ/(kg$\cdot$K), $r=2.3$ MJ/kg.
In which resistance is the most heat released? $R_1=1~\Omega, R_2=R_3=2~\Omega, R_4=4~\Omega$. (See the figure)

A boiler (immersion heater) of resistance $R_1$ boils a certain amount of water in time $t_1$. A boiler of resistance $R_2$ boils the same water under the same conditions in time $t_2$. In what time will the water boil if both boilers are connected in parallel?

An electric kettle has two heating coils. When the first coil is connected, the water boils in time $t_1$; when the second is connected, in time $t_2$. How many times longer is the boiling time when both coils are connected in series than when they are connected in parallel?
If two identical electric hotplates are connected in parallel, water boils in time $t$. In what time will the same water boil if the hotplates are connected in series?

An electric kettle has two heating coils. When one of them is connected, the water in the kettle boils in $30$ minutes; when the other is connected, it boils in $20$ minutes. In how many minutes will the water in the kettle boil if both coils are connected in series?

An electric heater has three identical branches of resistance $R$ each. If all three branches are connected in parallel, the water in a vessel placed on it boils in $6$ min. In how many minutes would the same water boil if the branches were connected in series?

An electric hotplate boils water in $10$ minutes. After part of the coil burned out, it boiled the same water in $12$ min. By what fraction of its original length was the coil shortened? Assume the current is constant.

Water is heated by two identical coils. At first the coils were connected in parallel to a DC voltage source for a time $t$, then in series for the same time. If during the first time $t$ the water temperature rose by $10^\circ$C, by how much did it rise during the total time $2t$ ($^\circ$C)?
How many joules is the unit of energy $1$ kilowatt-hour equal to?
In one room of a student dormitory, a $100$ W light bulb is on for $6$ hours every day. If $1$ kW$\cdot$h of electricity costs $450$ soums, how much will its monthly ($30$ days) cost be (soums)?

What power (kW) must a consumer connected to the mains have for the rotation frequency of the electric meter disk to equal $1.5$ Hz? ($3000$ revolutions of the disk correspond to $1$ kW$\cdot$h of energy.)

When an electrical appliance is connected to the mains, the disk of the electric meter makes $30$ revolutions in one minute. What is the power of this appliance (kW)? (The meter states that $1$ kW$\cdot$h corresponds to $1200$ revolutions of the disk.)
The power of a fan installed in a room is $36$ W. What work does it do in $20$ s (J)?
How much work (MJ) can a power plant with a power of $500$ kW do in one hour?
How much energy (kJ) does an electric kettle with an electric power of $0.5$ kW consume in $5$ minutes?
Which formula is used to calculate the work of a direct current?
Which of the given relations express the work of an electric current? 1) $A=Nt$; 2) $A=Fscos\alpha$; 3) $A=q(\varphi_1-\varphi_2)$; 4) $A=IUt$; 5) $A=I^2Rt$.
What is the name of the physical quantity whose unit can be written as J/(A$^2\cdot$s)?
In a part of a circuit with a voltage of $200$ V, the current did $16$ kJ of work. How many electrons passed through this part?
A conductor of resistance $20~\Omega$ has a voltage of $20$ V applied to its ends. How many joules of work does the current do in $20$ seconds?
If the voltage across a part of a circuit is $3$ V, how many joules of work does a current of $6$ A do in it in $10$ s?
At what voltage (in volts) across a part of a circuit does a current of $3$ A do, in $4$ s, $24$ J of work in that part?
In $3$ s an electric current does $6$ J of work in a part of a circuit. If the voltage across that part of the circuit is $2$ V, find the current flowing through it (A).

What is the SI unit of the quantity defined by the expression $j^2\rho lS$? ($j$ is the current density, $\rho$ is the resistivity of the conductor, $l$ and $S$ are the length and cross-sectional area of the conductor).
Which physical quantity is determined by the following expression? $\frac{P}{j^2\rho}$ $P$ is power, $j$ is current density, $\rho$ is resistivity.
An incandescent lamp bulb is marked $4$ V and $0.25$ A. Find the resistance ($\Omega$) and power (W) of the lamp during operation.
The base of an incandescent lamp is marked $250$ V, $25$ W. What is the resistance of this lamp ($\Omega$)?
An incandescent lamp bulb is marked $3.5$ V and $0.28$ A. Find the operating resistance and power of the lamp.
An electric lamp of $72$ W power is designed for a voltage of $12$ V. Determine the resistance of the lamp ($\Omega$).
The power of an electric lamp designed for a voltage of $12$ V is $60$ W. Determine the resistance of the lamp ($\Omega$).
The power of an electric hotplate is $1$ kW. If a current of $5$ A flows through the coil of the hotplate, what is the resistance of the coil (in $\Omega$)?
What is the maximum voltage (in volts) that can be applied to a resistor rated for a power of $1$ W with a resistance of $1~\Omega$?

How many meters of nichrome wire must be taken to make a heater designed for a voltage of $36$ V and a power of $180$ W, if the cross-sectional area of the wire is $0.6$ mm$^2$? The resistivity of nichrome is $\rho=1.2\cdot10^{-6}~\Omega\cdot$m.
Using the graph of current versus applied voltage, determine the power (W) dissipated in this part of the circuit at a voltage of $40$ V.
When an electric hotplate was repaired, its coil was shortened to $0.2$ of its original length. How does its power change? $U=\text{const}$.
For two bulbs of equal power designed for voltages $U_1=6$ V and $U_2=12$ V, what is the ratio of their resistances $(R_1/R_2)$?
For electric lamps of equal power designed for voltages $U_1=24$ V and $U_2=8$ V, find the ratio of their resistances $(R_1/R_2)$.
Each of two lamps is designed for a voltage of $220$ V. The power of one of the lamps is $P_1=50$ W and of the other $P_2=150$ W. Find the ratio of the resistances of these lamps $R_2/R_1$.
How are the resistances of two lamps designed for the same voltage related if their powers are $P_1=2P_2$?
Two electric heaters are connected in parallel to the mains. The resistance of the first heater is $50~\Omega$ and that of the second is $20~\Omega$. Find the ratio of the heaters' powers $P_1/P_2$.
Two resistors with resistances $R_1=2~\Omega$ and $R_2=8~\Omega$ are connected in parallel to a current source. Compare the powers $P_1$ and $P_2$ of the current in these resistors.
When the voltage across the ends of a circuit was increased $1.5$ times, the dissipated power increased $6$ times. Did the current in the circuit change?
How does the power of the current change if the voltage across the ends of a circuit with constant resistance is increased $6$ times?
How does the power of the current in a conductor change if the voltage across its ends is increased $4$ times?
How does the power of the current change if, at constant voltage, the electrical resistance is decreased $5$ times?
In an electric network, two electric lamps with resistances of $100~\Omega$ and $200~\Omega$ are connected in parallel. Which lamp consumes more power?
answers: the second, by a factor of 2.
the first, by a factor of 2.
the second, by a factor of 4.
the first, by a factor of 4.

questions.text: How does the power of the current change if, at constant voltage, the electrical resistance is decreased $2$ times?
How does the power of the current change if, at constant current, the electrical resistance is decreased $2$ times?
Two identical resistors were connected to a DC voltage supply first in parallel and then in series. In which case is the power of the current greater, and by what factor?
answers: in series, by a factor of 2.
in parallel, by a factor of 2.
in series, by a factor of 4.
in parallel, by a factor of 4.

questions.text: If the power dissipated in resistor $R_1$ is $40$ W, the voltage across it is $10$ V, the current in resistor $R_2$ is $2$ A, and the resistance of resistor $R_3$ is $4~\Omega$, what is the total resistance of the circuit ($\Omega$)?
To a voltage source $U$ a resistance $R$ is connected. If a resistance $2R$ is connected in series, how does the power in the resistance $R$ change?
What resistance must be connected in series with a resistance $R$ connected to a constant voltage so that the power in it (in the resistance $R$) decreases $2.25$ times?
An electric motor does $1080$ kJ of useful work in one hour and consumes $0.4$ kW$\cdot$h of energy. What is its efficiency (in %)?
A water heater with a power of $1$ kW transfers, in $5$ min, $100$ kJ of heat to the water. What is the efficiency of this heater?
An elevator with a mass of $1000$ kg rose uniformly in $0,025$ hours to a height of $81$ m. If the efficiency of the elevator is $90\%$, what power does the motor consume (kW)?
At a current of $110$ A and a voltage of $600$ V, a tram car produces a traction force of $3$ kN. If the efficiency is $60\%$, at what speed (m/s) does the tram move on a horizontal track?

An electric locomotive, powered from a $1.5$ kV mains, at a speed of $18$ m/s produces a traction force of $45$ kN. If the efficiency of the locomotive's motors is $90\%$, what is the total current in them (in amperes)?
Find the power of the second iron in this electric circuit (W).
How does the power dissipated in the circuit change if switch $K$ in the diagram is closed?
The figure shows $4$ light bulbs connected to a voltage source. In which bulb is the greatest power dissipated? Find this power if $U=100$ V.
What is the power of the electric current in the circuit given in the diagram (W)? $U=12$ V, $R_1=7~\Omega$, $R_2=5~\Omega$, $R_3=R_5=4~\Omega$, $R_4=9~\Omega$.
